text: {"side":"artifact","claims":[{"text":"The event's points come mostly from soft-rejected, standard-soft plates: 23 of 26 points are flagged STD_SOFT, so the lightcurve rests on a degraded measurement class rather than clean detections.","evidence_ids":["E-064","E-031","E-032","E-033"]},{"text":"One of the event's points is flagged EMULSION_UNKNOWN, meaning its emulsion response is not characterized and the point could reflect an emulsion effect rather than a stellar change.","evidence_ids":["E-058","E-036"]},{"text":"The ee series has a median zero-point offset of -1.843 mag from only 3 plates, and many event points come from ee plates with offsets near -1.9, so a series-level calibration seam could produce the apparent dip.","evidence_ids":["E-023","E-033","E-034","E-039","E-052"]},{"text":"The lightcurve is not detrended and the star is flagged as a known variable, so a plate-to-plate or known periodic signal could account for the apparent outburst without requiring an artifact or a new event.","evidence_ids":["E-067","E-068"]},{"text":"The packet does not include the 1946 plate-level checks needed to rule out a seam or a missing point: no series overlap comparison and no detrended curve are provided, so an artifact explanation cannot be confirmed or excluded from this evidence alone.","evidence_ids":["E-066","E-067","E-002"]}]}
